 Order
T h i s first bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed on behalf of applicant for grant of bail, pending the trial.

The applicant has been arrested in connection with Crime No.710/2022 o f Police Station Majholi,
District Sidhi (M.P.) for commission of offence under Section 376(2)(n) of IPC.
He is in detention since 23.07.2022.

As per prosecution story, on 22.07.2022, 20 year old prosecutrix filed an application in writing alleging that applicant Salman Khan established physical relations with her on the promise of marriage and now he has denied to solemnize marriage with her.
FIR was registered.
After investigation, charge sheet has been filed.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
Applicant and prosecutrix, both are major and are from the same community.
They were having consensual sexual relationship.
Prosecutrix has already been examined before the trial Court.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
O n the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed grant of bail to the applicant.
In trial, prosecutrix has already been examined before the trial Court.
Trial of the case will take considerable time.
Having considered the overall facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pretrial detention of the applicant/accused is not warranted.
Consequently, this first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

It is directed that applicant - Salman Khan be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
